# Piton fluency

Piton is a declarative, whitespace-structured language for describing agentic
skills, agents, commands, and reference documents. It has no runtime: it
compiles to data (JSON, YAML) or, through a framework, to Markdown. Source
files use the `.pi` extension.

## Syntax

```piton
// A comment. Comments are line-only.
myVariable: 42                       // a number
myString: Strings are unquoted       // a string
myQuoted: "false"                    // quoting forces a string
myTyped:: string:: number: 42        // constraints, first match wins

myList:
    - one
    - two
myInlineList: [one, two, three]

myDictionary:
    nested:
        deep: value

computed: {1 + 2}                    // `{ }` evaluates; bare text does not
interpolated: Hello, ${myString}

anchor Base:
    name: Base
    summary: This is ${this.name}  // `this` pins to Base

anchor Child extends Base:
    name: Child
    detail: This is ${self.name}   // `self` follows the child
    summary: ${super.summary} and more

abstract anchor Shape as shape:      // `as` registers a keyword
    description:: string

shape Concrete:                      // same as `extends Shape`
    description: Implemented

from ./other import Thing, Other Alias
from ./other export *
use ./keywords
export anchor Published:
    value: 1
```

## Reserved words

`anchor`, `abstract`, `extends`, `as`, `export`, `from`, `import`, `use`, `this`, `self`, `super`, `true`, `false`, `null`

## Types

`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `list`, `dictionary`, `anchor`, `any`, `simple`, `complex`

Literals: `true`, `false`, `null`

## Rules worth memorising

- A value is an expression only when the *whole* value parses as one over
  literal atoms. `1 + 2` is `3`; `a + b` is the string `a + b`; use `{a + b}`
  to reference names.
- `+` on lists concatenates and deduplicates, right operand winning:
  `[1,2,3,4] + [1,2,3]` is `[4,1,2,3]`. `++` keeps duplicates.
- `+` merges dictionaries shallowly; `++` merges them deeply.
- Mixing unrelated types with `+` produces a mixed list, not an error.
- A block that mixes prose, `- ` items, and `key:` pairs becomes an implicit
  list; the keys written directly in it stay addressable.
- Inheritance is left to right with the right-most base winning; a child always
  wins over its bases; a declaring keyword is the left-most base.
- A concrete anchor may implement at most one abstract anchor, and must supply
  every abstract property left without a value.
- Strings never coerce to `boolean` or `number`; simple values do coerce to
  `string`.
- Modulo uses floor semantics; division by zero and comparing mismatched types
  are compile errors.
- Two files may import from each other. A circular reference is an error only
  when it cannot settle: `${A}` and `${B}` naming each other is fine, because an
  interpolated anchor renders as its name, while `A: {B}` and `B: {A}` is not.
- Indentation must be consistent within a file; the canonical style is four
  spaces.

## Frameworks

### `@piton/belay` (framework `belay`)

`use @piton/belay` for its keywords, `from @piton/belay import ...` for its anchors.

Interpolation sigils: `@{}`

- **Agent** (abstract anchor) — keyword `agent`
  - `description:: string`
  - `role:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **Skill** (abstract anchor) — keyword `skill`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
  - `useWhen:: string`
- **Command** (abstract anchor) — keyword `command`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **Instruction** (abstract anchor) — keyword `instruction`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **SelfInstruction** (abstract anchor) — keyword `self-instruction`
  - `description:: string`
  - `prompt:: string`
- **BelayConfig** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-config`
  - `codeRoot:: string`
- **Adapter** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-adapter`
  - `description:: string`
- **AgentAdapter** (abstract anchor) — keyword `belay-agent-adapter`
  - `description:: string`
- **ClaudeAdapter** (anchor)
  - `description`
  - `claude`
- **OpenCodeAdapter** (anchor)
  - `description`
  - `opencode`
- **__BELAY_SHAPE__** (variable)

## Working with a Piton project

- `piton check <glob>` reports errors without writing anything.
- `piton compile <glob>` writes JSON or YAML next to each input.
- `piton build` builds the project described by `piton.config.pi`.
- `piton build check` builds and reports without writing.
- `piton format <glob>` applies the canonical style: four spaces, one space
  after `//`, sorted and wrapped import lists.
- `piton lsp` runs the language server.

## Writing Piton well

- Prefer an abstract anchor exported `as` a keyword for anything that will be
  implemented repeatedly; it documents intent and prevents a concrete anchor
  from implementing two abstracts.
- Reach for `+ {super.x}` rather than repeating a base's list.
- Use `this` when a base wants its own value and `self` when it wants the
  most-derived one.
- Keep prose as prose. Only reach for `{ }` when a value genuinely needs to be
  computed or referenced.
----

use /lib
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from ../prompt-mode import PromptEditor
from ../prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from ../harness-stream import HarnessStream
from ../editor import EditorScope
from ../palette import PaletteScope

export scope MainWindowScope:
    concept: {MainWindowConcept}

concept MainWindowConcept:
    pitch:
        The main window of the application allowing you interact with all main
        functionality.

    shape: {MainWindowShape}

shape MainWindowShape:
    description:
        Maximized window.

    darkMode:
        The whole window, including popups and notifications, supports a light
        and a dark theme.

        A "Dark mode" switch at the far right of the toolbar toggles between the
        two.

        The choice is persistent: it is saved for the user, across all
        projects, and restored on the next launch. Until a choice has been
        made, the window follows the operating system's light or dark
        appearance.

    escape:
        Pressing Esc anywhere in the window, including in an @{EditorScope}, moves
        focus to the @{ChatInputScope}. Esc first closes whatever it would
        otherwise dismiss, such as a completion menu or a popup.

    palette:
        Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) opens the @{PaletteScope} over the window, for
        fuzzy searching the project's files, the application's own commands,
        and the harness's commands, skills, and agents.

    header:
        toolbar:
            Toolbar on top that contains a button for @{ProjectDirectoryScope}
            As well as a Build button that will run `piton build`

            In the middle of the toolbar, a toggle button shows or hides a
            @{HarnessStream} split view beside prompt mode. It reads
            "View Raw Output" while the split is hidden and "Hide Raw Output"
            while it is shown.

    body:
        sidebar:
            A sidebar along the left of the body displays a tree view of the
            current @{ProjectDirectoryScope}. Folders are listed before files,
            both by name, and a folder's contents are shown when it is
            expanded. The tree refreshes by itself when files or folders are
            added, removed, or renamed on disk, keeping expanded folders open
            and the selection in place. The sidebar is resized by dragging its
            edge. Until a project is picked it reads "No project open".

        openFile:
            Clicking a file in the tree opens it in an @{EditorScope}, in a
            split beside the chat history: the file on the left taking 50% of
            the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The split
            can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes the
            split. The @{ChatInputScope} is never split: it stays along the
            bottom, across the full width of prompt mode.

        promptMode:
            The body displays the @{PromptEditor} and any splits, to the
            right of the sidebar.

21	        results beneath that.

24	        Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) anywhere in the window opens the palette on the

29	        Picking a result closes the palette. Esc clears the search, and closes
30	        the palette once the search is empty. Clicking outside the palette
31	        closes it. Closing it without picking anything puts focus back where it
32	        was.
33	
34	    tabs:
35	        overview:
36	            The tabs are Files, System, Commands, Skills, and Agents, in that
37	            order. Each lists its own results. The search is kept when switching
38	            tabs, and applies to the tab switched to.
39	
40	        switching:
41	            Clicking a tab switches to it. <Tab> moves to the next tab and
42	            <Shift+Tab> to the previous one, wrapping around, and focus stays in
43	            the search field.

46	            Every file in the selected @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, at any depth,
47	            listed by its path in the project. `.git`, and whatever the
48	            project's `.gitignore` files ignore, are left out. Picking a file
49	            opens it in the @{EditorScope}, as clicking it in the project tree
50	            does. Until a project is picked the tab reads "No project open".
51

53	            The application's own commands, each doing what its toolbar control
54	            or shortcut does: "Open Project…", "Build", "View Raw Output" or
55	            "Hide Raw Output", "Dark mode" or "Light mode" (whichever is not
56	            the current one), and "Quit". Build is unavailable while there is

69	            after `@`.

73	            Picking one inserts it into the @{ChatInputScope} at the cursor the
74	            way accepting it as a mention does, `/name ` for a command or skill
75	            and `@agent-name ` for an agent, with a space before it when the

79	        A result matches when the search's characters all appear in it in

81	        best matches come first: runs of consecutive characters, and characters

83	        results. The matched characters are highlighted. With an empty search,
84	        files are listed by path, the application's commands in the order
85	        above, and the harness's by name. At most the 100 best results are
86	        listed.

90	        Enter picks the highlighted result. Clicking a result picks it.

        harness's commands, skills, and agents.

    shape: {PaletteShape}

shape PaletteShape:
    description:
        A popover near the top of the window, over a dimmed backdrop: a tab bar
        using gpui-kit's default tab styling, a search field beneath it, and the
        results beneath that.

    opening:
        Ctrl+P (Cmd+P on macOS) anywhere in the window opens the palette on the
        Files tab with an empty search and focus in the search field. Pressing
        it again while the palette is open closes it.

    closing:
        Picking a result closes the palette. Esc clears the search, and closes
        the palette once the search is empty. Clicking outside the palette
        closes it. Closing it without picking anything puts focus back where it
        was.

    tabs:
        overview:
            The tabs are Files, System, Commands, Skills, and Agents, in that
            order. Each lists its own results. The search is kept when switching
            tabs, and applies to the tab switched to.

        switching:
            Clicking a tab switches to it. <Tab> moves to the next tab and
            <Shift+Tab> to the previous one, wrapping around, and focus stays in
            the search field.

        files:
            Every file in the selected @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, at any depth,
            listed by its path in the project. `.git`, and whatever the
            project's `.gitignore` files ignore, are left out. Picking a file
            opens it in the @{EditorScope}, as clicking it in the project tree
            does. Until a project is picked the tab reads "No project open".

        system:
            The application's own commands, each doing what its toolbar control
            or shortcut does: "Open Project…", "Build", "View Raw Output" or
            "Hide Raw Output", "Dark mode" or "Light mode" (whichever is not
            the current one), and "Quit". Build is unavailable while there is
            no project or a build is running.

        commands:
            The harness's commands, the same ones the @{ChatInputScope} offers
            after `/`.

        skills:
            The harness's skills, the same ones the @{ChatInputScope} offers
            after `/`.

        agents:
            The harness's agents, the same ones the @{ChatInputScope} offers
            after `@`.

        mentions:
            A command, skill, or agent shows its description when it has one.
            Picking one inserts it into the @{ChatInputScope} at the cursor the
            way accepting it as a mention does, `/name ` for a command or skill
            and `@agent-name ` for an agent, with a space before it when the
            cursor follows other text. Focus then moves to the chat input.

    fuzzySearch:
        A result matches when the search's characters all appear in it in
        order, ignoring case, though not necessarily next to each other. The
        best matches come first: runs of consecutive characters, and characters
        at the start of a word or of a file's name, rank higher, then shorter
        results. The matched characters are highlighted. With an empty search,
        files are listed by path, the application's commands in the order
        above, and the harness's by name. At most the 100 best results are
        listed.

    keyboard:
        Up and Down move the highlight, which starts on the first result, and
        Enter picks the highlighted result. Clicking a result picks it.

use /lib
from /scope/lsp import LSP

export scope EditorScope:
    concept: {EditorConcept}

concept EditorConcept:
    pitch:
        An editor for a file opened from the project tree, with language
        support for Piton files.

    shape: {EditorShape}

shape EditorShape:
    description:
        Editable and syntax highlighted, under a header with the file's path
        in the project, a dot while it has unsaved changes, a save button, and
        a close button.

    saving:
        Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) or the save button writes the file to disk.
        A file that cannot be saved keeps its changes and says why beneath
        the header.

    languageSupport:
        overview:
            A Piton file (`.pi`) is edited with the project's @{LSP} server,
            shared with the chat input, which sees the editor's unsaved text:
            the file is opened with `textDocument/didOpen`, kept current with
            full-text `textDocument/didChange`, reported with
            `textDocument/didSave` when saved, and closed with
            `textDocument/didClose` when the editor closes or shows another
            file. Other files are edited without language support, as is a
            Piton file while the server is not running.

        completions:
            `textDocument/completion` is requested after typing a letter, a
            digit, an opening curly brace, a period, a dollar sign, an at
            sign, a colon, or an underscore, and narrowed and ordered as in
            the chat input. Accepting a completion also applies the import the
            server attaches to it.

        hover:
            Hovering a name shows the server's `textDocument/hover`.

        definitions:
            Ctrl-clicking (Cmd-clicking on macOS) a name goes to its
            `textDocument/definition`. A definition in another file opens that
            file in the editor, at the definition.

        diagnostics:
            What the server publishes for the file is underlined, with the
            message shown on hover, and kept while the text is edited until
            the server publishes again.

        quickFixes:
            Ctrl+. (Cmd+. on macOS) lists the server's
            `textDocument/codeAction` fixes at the cursor, and picking one
            applies its edits to the file.

    replacing:
        Opening another file shows that file in its place. While there are
        unsaved changes, it first asks whether to discard them.

    closing:
        A close button above the file closes it. While there are unsaved
        changes, it first asks whether to discard them.

        two.

        The choice is persistent: it is saved for the user, across all
        projects, and restored on the next launch. Until a choice has been
        made, the window follows the operating system's light or dark
        appearance.

    escape:
        Pressing Esc anywhere in the window, including in an @{EditorScope}, moves

            bottom, across the full width of prompt mode.

        promptMode:
            The body displays the @{PromptEditor} and any splits, to the
            right of the sidebar.

content.text:
I added a `gitStatus` section to the sidebar part of the spec, in `spec/scope/application/MainWindow.pi` right after `sidebar`. `piton check` and `piton build check` both pass. I didn't change anything in `./src`.

What it says:
- **Colors:** in a git repository, modified, added, untracked and conflicted files each get their own color. Ignored files and folders are dimmed, and unchanged ones keep the normal color.
- **Folders:** a folder takes the most urgent status of anything inside it, in the order conflicted, modified, added, untracked. That way a change still shows when the folder is collapsed.
- **Themes:** the colors have to work in both light and dark mode.
- **Refreshing:** the colors update on their own when files change on disk or the repository changes, such as after staging, committing or switching branches.
- **No repository:** if the project isn't in a git repository, the tree has no highlighting.

Some choices you may want to change:
- **Deleted files** aren't covered, because the tree only lists what's on disk.
- **Staged vs. unstaged** changes look the same.
- **Actual colors** aren't named; the spec only says each status gets its own.
- **Renamed files** have no status of their own.
